claim: For every admissible finite D, every positive cutoff k and finite deletion F as in the all-future prefix-surplus claim, there is an integer L>=0 such that for every integer M>=1 there is m>=M with S_m>=2L and every integer in [L,S_m-L] a subset sum of the first m remaining labelled occurrences.

quadruple.statement: For every admissible D,k,F there exists one integer L>=0 such that for every M>=1 there exists m>=M with S_m>=2L and [z^n] product_{i=1}^m (1+z^{a_i})>0 for every integer L<=n<=S_m-L.
quadruple.stage: Exact integer coefficients of finite labelled pure-power products, with equivalent tilted lattice Fourier inversion.

shape.objects: Finite distinct base sets, positive cutoffs, finite labelled deletions, infinite locally finite sorted power streams, and finite sets of binary selections. The underlying Nat powers, finite products, finite sums, polynomials and limits have standard Lean/Mathlib definitions. Once a compatible represented central seed is supplied, adding successive unused labels amplifies it under the recorded all-future surplus condition. The bases and labels are rigid; there is no continuous deformation of the original objects. A Bernoulli distribution on the finite label selections is available as a prospective auxiliary object, not a proved coverage estimate.
shape.quantifiers: For every admissible D,k,F there exists one integer L>=0, for every M>=1 there exists m>=M with the stated nonempty represented central interval; L is fixed while m is unbounded. The leading input quantifiers are universal; the inner existence asks for a cover of all integers in each selected finite central interval.
shape.target_quantity: A qualitative existence and coverage property, not a numerical optimum, density bound or exponent. An unspecified finite endpoint loss L and unbounded suitable prefix indices suffice. A finite run does not determine the all-input existence of this constant.
shape.ambient_structure: Additive integer order and multiplicative power structure coexist. Finite generating polynomials and exact Fourier coefficients encode lattice representation without discarding individual labels. Prefix addition is the available amplification operation, conditional on a seed and a surplus inequality. No closed family of structured pieces with a bias statistic is recorded. A bound for dependence between the proposed full-coverage probability events is unknown; it must not be inferred merely from independence of the input bits. No transport path to a solved member is available.
shape.symmetries: Base relabelling preserves the assertion and numerical ties retain separate labels. Complementing a finite label selection reflects its sum about half the prefix total. No structured-piece family closed under the translations, dilations and intersections required by a density-increment argument has been supplied.
shape.configuration: Every integer in a fixed-loss central interval must be a sum of distinct labelled powers. This is an additive relation between a finite binary selection and its numerical sum, not a configuration-avoidance density problem. A represented central interval can be destroyed by moving to another prefix without the matching surplus inequality, as the recorded early-seed examples show. The conditional prefix-amplification operation must preserve the central integer interval and the one fixed loss.
shape.extremal_candidate: No extremal counterexample in the pure-power class or opposite-side construction with a target bound is known. An abstract sequence counterexample is accepted but is not an admissible power stream.
shape.finite_certificates: A specified finite prefix and represented interval can be checked exactly, so small illustrative instances are computable in principle. Neither the universal seed statement nor its negation has a known finite certificate. No bounded smallest-seed search domain or finite-residue execution is admitted, including at strict mass. The equality-case supplied surplus threshold is ineffective.
shape.monotonicity: For a fixed stream, increasing a fixed L weakens the interval-coverage requirement once S_m>=2L, and S_m grows without bound. The theorem quantifies over unbounded cutoffs and prefixes. No smallest unresolved finite cutoff or complete finite range has been established.
shape.uniformity_parameter: All admissible finite D, all positive cutoffs k and all finite deletions F; one L must work for arbitrarily late prefixes of each input, including reciprocal equality. It may depend on D,k,F but not on the selected prefix.
shape.proof_shape: The exact statement has explicit hypotheses and quantifiers. The proposed argument is a chain: translate to exact finite generating-function coefficients, test a coefficient-positivity mechanism using the actual powers, pull back fixed-loss seed coverage, and only then use accepted surplus for propagation. No proof of the seed, complete informal proof chain, finite solver step, two independent numerical-loss interfaces, or sum bounded by an already selected free auxiliary weight is recorded. The previously stopped methods do not define a new formal class on which a barrier theorem is being claimed.
shape.neighbours: Known true under stronger density assumptions: Cassels's circle-method completeness criterion, as stated in the primary Bergelson-Simmons and Fan papers and the zbMATH review. Known true: exact coefficient extraction for finite binary-sum generating polynomials, and zero-cutoff Brown interval coverage. Known false: the already accepted abstract all-sublinear-surplus arithmetic inference. Open here: the exact pure-power seed claim, C1, and fixed-D all-cutoff special cases such as D={3,4,5}. Finite initial illustrative instances of these neighbours are checkable. No simpler ambient carries the full seed statement verbatim while dropping the integer lattice, and no reflection-preserving transport to a solved family has been supplied.
shape.known_bounds: Accepted checkpoint-000009 proves S_m-a_(m+1) tends to positive infinity for all inputs. The direct interval method still lacks a compatible fixed-loss seed, and its attempted early seeds fail. Pure counting of labelled subsets and the earlier real-image method do not prove exact coverage. Cassels's dyadic growth assumption is absent for finite power unions. Fan's three bounded-deficit components are not established by the total reciprocal mass condition. No finite counterexample compression, complete finite residue, all-input seed constant, or independently movable quantitative ledger is recorded. A suitable first-moment coverage bound is unknown. The prospective local coefficient estimate has not been separated from the substantive seed difficulty by a proved independent theorem. Move 1 gives an elementary proof candidate that the uniform standardized prefix sums cannot have a Gaussian limit for fixed finite D: E[Y_m^4]<=3-2/C_D^2 with C_D=sum_d (1-d^-2)^-1 and uniform fourth-moment integrability. This is not independently accepted. Exact coefficient extraction and the per-base functional equation do not yet yield positivity; the scalar prefix recurrence meets the same seed obstruction.
shape.missing_input: A non-Gaussian, lattice-scale coefficient positivity mechanism using the actual distinct pure-power factors; neither the exact product identity nor its per-base recursion presently supplies one. The Gaussian obstruction is a local proof candidate, not accepted root evidence.
shape.base_theory: Classical mathematics in ZFC on finite and countable objects. The standard classical Lean axioms cover the intended foundations; any later finite check would have to stay within the separately admitted proof policy. No uncountable threshold, forcing axiom, guessing principle, or independence statement is available or needed.

known: Accepted analytical surplus theorem: checkpoint-000009, acceptance-000002, node-000005 move 1. Its published input is ESS, arXiv:math/0409604v1, DOI 10.2307/3062133; it proves no represented seed.
BEGL96, DOI 10.4064/aa-77-2-133-138: original positive-cutoff conjecture, cutoff-dependent finite base subsets and specified k=1 examples; not an all-input seed theorem.
Bergelson-Simmons arXiv:1507.02208v2, DOI 10.4064/aa8221-10-2016, Section 2: exact disjoint-supply completeness criterion and Cassels comparison.
Steve Fan, arXiv:2607.14071v1, Sections 1-2 through Corollary 2.5: finite-support refinement to three bounded-deficit components; its hypotheses are not supplied for all pure-power streams.
Cassels 1960, Acta Sci. Math. 21, 111-124, zbMATH 3345481: circle-method route under stronger density conditions; exact original full paper not inspected or imported.
Canonical root Erdos124.erdos124.ne_zero in sources/124.lean, read against the immutable root quantifiers; live https://www.erdosproblems.com/124 inspected 2026-09-07.
